findings.issue_text: Guest emails are not deduplicated, allowing duplicate attendee records and duplicate calendar/email recipients
Attendees are committed before calendar synchronization, so a calendar failure leaves the database changed and retries fail, causing permanent divergence
Blacklist comparison does not normalize submitted email casing, allowing mixed-case blocked addresses to bypass the blacklist
The handler permits adding guests even when the event type has guest additions disabled
Team-admin and team-owner authorization is combined with AND instead of OR, incorrectly denying either role alone
Calendar updates use the caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's, targeting the wrong calendar or no calendar
Adding guests updates Booking.attendees but leaves responses.guests stale
Email notifications use the original guest input instead of filtered unique guests, misclassifying existing attendees as new-booking confirmations

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Attendees are committed before calendar synchronization, so a calendar failure leaves the database changed and retries fail, causing permanent divergence

adjudication.rationale: Looking at addGuests.handler.ts, the code first updates the database with new attendees (lines 85-99 with prisma.booking.update), then later calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking) to sync with the calendar. If the calendar update fails, the database already has the new attendees committed, but the calendar doesn't. This is a real atomicity issue - there's no transaction wrapping both operations, and no rollback of the database changes if the calendar sync fails. The code does have a try-catch around sendAddGuestsEmails but not around updateCalendarAttendees, so calendar failures would throw and leave the system in an inconsistent state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The handler permits adding guests even when the event type has guest additions disabled

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the addGuests.handler.ts code, the handler checks if the user is a team admin/owner, organizer, or attendee before allowing guest additions. However, there is no check for whether the event type has guest additions enabled (e.g., checking booking.eventType.disableGuests or similar property). The handler only validates permissions but not the event type's guest policy settings. This is a real missing validation - if an event type is configured to not allow guests, this handler would still permit adding guests after the booking is created.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar updates use the caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's, targeting the wrong calendar or no calendar

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the addGuests.handler.ts, the code gets credentials from the current user (ctx.user) via `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and creates an EventManager with those credentials. However, the booking may have been created by a different organizer (booking.user). The code does fetch booking.user with credentials included, but then uses ctx.user's credentials for the EventManager. This means if an attendee or team admin (who is not the organizer) adds guests, the calendar update will use their credentials instead of the organizer's credentials, which could target the wrong calendar or fail if they don't have calendar integration set up.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Adding guests updates Booking.attendees but leaves responses.guests stale

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the addGuests.handler.ts creates new attendees in the database via prisma.booking.update with attendees.createMany, but there is no code that updates any 'responses.guests' field. However, examining the diff carefully, I don't see any evidence that a 'responses.guests' field exists or is used in this codebase. The booking model shown includes 'attendees' as the relationship for guests. The finding assumes there's a separate 'responses.guests' field that needs to be kept in sync, but this is not demonstrated in the diff. Without evidence that such a field exists and is used elsewhere, this finding appears to be speculation about code structure not shown in the diff.
